58	\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
59	\label{sec:discussion}
60	\input{section7_conclusion_compressed}
61	
62	% === Limitations (ARR requirement: standalone section, does not count toward page limit) ===
63	\section*{Limitations}
64	
65	The semantic layer introduces cross-field consistency (CF) violations (up to 12.02\%), a systematic consequence of per-relation independent enforcement that remains an open challenge.
66	Entity F1 impact is model-dependent ($+$1.22\,pp for Qwen vs.\ $-$0.64\,pp for Llama on DocRED), partially confounded by increased parse failures under constraints (Llama: 9.1\% vs.\ 6.8\%).
67	Results cover two 8B-class models under zero-shot prompting, where relation F1 remains around 8\% compared to $\sim$50\% for fine-tuned systems.
68	The framework is model-agnostic and can be composed with fine-tuned models, but this combination has not been empirically validated.
69	The semantic layer's dynamic masking assumes each entity type maps to a unique first subword token---verified for both tokenizers on our two ontologies (6 entity types each), but ontologies with many types or multi-token type names would require prefix-tree masking, which we have not implemented.
70	Global entity-level type consensus during decoding offers the most direct path to resolving CF violations.
71	Validation with fine-tuned models, larger scales, and non-English ontologies remains to be explored.
72

      "content": "\\section{Discussion and Conclusion}\n\\label{sec:discussion}\n\\input{section7_conclusion_compressed}\n\n% === Limitations (ARR requirement: standalone section, does not count toward page limit) ===\n\\section*{Limitations}\n\nThe semantic layer introduces cross-field consistency (CF) violations (up to 12.02\\%), a systematic consequence of per-relation independent enforcement that remains an open challenge.\nEntity F1 impact is model-dependent ($+$1.22\\,pp for Qwen vs.\\ $-$0.64\\,pp for Llama on DocRED), partially confounded by increased parse failures under constraints (Llama: 9.1\\% vs.\\ 6.8\\%).\nResults cover two 8B-class models under zero-shot prompting, where relation F1 remains around 8\\% compared to $\\sim$50\\% for fine-tuned systems.\nThe framework is model-agnostic and can be composed with fine-tuned models, but this combination has not been empirically validated.\nThe semantic layer's dynamic masking assumes each entity type maps to a unique first subword token---verified for both tokenizers on our two ontologies (6 entity types each), but ontologies with many types or multi-token type names would require prefix-tree masking, which we have not implemented.\nGlobal entity-level type consensus during decoding offers the most direct path to resolving CF violations.\nValidation with fine-tuned models, larger scales, and non-English ontologies remains to be explored.\n",
